sources.title: Jean-Luc Vellut, África Central do Oeste em Vésperas da Partilha Colonial (1980)
sources.note: Original historical study, África 3, pp. 73 to 120. Full indexed passages on pp. 102 to 103 checked; direct PDF fetch redirects repeatedly. Bibliographic identity independently checked against the USP issue contents. Source distinguishes eighteenth-century monopoly from nineteenth-century decentralization.

sources.title: José C. Curto, Jeribita in the Relations Between the Colony of Angola and the Kingdom of Kasanje (2013)
sources.note: Original archival study, Anais de História de Além-Mar XIV, pp. 301 to 325, directly read. Printed page numbers are one less than zero-based PDF page indices in this volume. Curto calls 1850 a conquest; Miller documents later regional autonomy and a 1912 endpoint. These are different stages, not a single uncontested fall date.

sources.title: David Livingstone, Missionary Travels and Researches in South Africa (1857), chapter 19
sources.note: Directly read transcription of the original travel account, describing April 1854 at Cassange. A foreign observer of a mixed trading settlement, not a census of Imbangala households. Writing quotation is his printed report of an Ambaca corporal’s letters, not an inspected surviving autograph.

sources.title: Joseph C. Miller, Kings, Lists, and History in Kasanje (1979)
sources.note: History in Africa 6, pp. 51 to 96. Publisher abstract and academic AfricaBib abstract checked; full JSTOR text not accessible. Precise pp. 51 and 54 passages on ca. 1620 to 1912, 1850s occupation and renewed regional factional power in the 1860s independently verified as quotations in Cambridge International Organization supplementary coding notes, https://static.cambridge.org/content/id/urn%3Acambridge.org%3Aid%3Aarticle%3AS0020818319000134/resource/name/S0020818319000134sup002.pdf . Do not claim direct full-paper access.

sources.title: Eva Sebestyén and Jan Vansina, Angola’s Eastern Hinterlands in the 1750s: edition of Manoel Correia Leitão’s voyage (1999)
sources.note: Original critical edition directly read. Editors identify unreliable travel claims, distances and numbers; only their positive assessment of the hoe-trading evidence is used, explicitly as earlier regional context.

sources.title: Maria da Conceição Neto, Bailundo: historical background and urbanism, HPIP
sources.note: Scholarly Portuguese built-heritage atlas. Full indexed text directly checked through web search; primary hostname direct fetch failed. Site gives Bailundo latitude -12.195169, unlike the displaced imported outline. Covers Ekwikwi II, 1896 destruction, 1902 revolt, 1904 district, schools and later urban infrastructure.

sources.title: Shana Melnysyn, Mbailundu Remembered: Colonial Traces in Post-Civil War Angola (2019)
sources.note: Original oral-history and archival research, Kronos 45, pp. 140 to 153. Full HTML directly read. Specific sections checked: 1884 and 1886 letters, Halavala court and 1895 fort, 2010 statue and the complications of its historical interpretation.

sources.title: Iracema Dulley, Chronicles of Bailundo: an Umbundu account of life before and after Portuguese rule (2021)
sources.note: Original critical edition directly read. Narrative recorded between 1903 and the 1930s; unidentified narrators and missionary compilers. Houghton Library HOU GEN 15.1, volume 44. Original Umbundu supplementary PDF 1 and Portuguese translation PDF 2 both directly checked at https://static.cambridge.org/content/id/urn:cambridge.org:id:article:S0001972021000553/resource/name/S0001972021000553sup001.pdf and corresponding sup002.pdf. All supplement-derived prose charged to this one work. Broad hostile claims about women or uncorroborated atrocities are not reproduced as facts.

sources.title: Jéssica Evelyn Pereira dos Santos, Guerra e sangue para uma colônia pacificada: a revolta do Bailundo (2016)
sources.note: Original historical study using administrative, missionary and press evidence. Publisher abstract directly read; article body unavailable. Only abstract-level finding used: heterogeneous groups in the 1902 to 1904 conflict and its role in extending Portuguese occupation.

sources.title: Wilfrid D. Hambly, The Ovimbundu of Angola (1934)
sources.note: Field Museum original expedition monograph, fieldwork 1929 to 1930, directly read in full searchable transcription. Colonial ethnographer: specific observed objects and practices are dated, not generalized as timeless or universal. Shared source across Bailundo and Ovimbundu cards; combined budget counted.

sources.title: Mariza de Carvalho Soares and Michele de Barcelos Agostinho, A coleção Ovimbundu do Museu Nacional, Angola 1929 to 1935 (2016)
sources.note: Original museum and archival research, Mana 22(2), pp. 493 onward, full article directly read. Used for changing Ovimbundu identity, specific school arrangements, 1916 Viovusenge title and translation, and 1926 bilingual hygiene book with named translators. Does not support a claim that hygiene itself was unknown before mission schools.

sources.title: Maria da Conceição Neto, In Town and Out of Town: A Social History of Huambo, 1902 to 1961 (2012)
sources.note: Original SOAS doctoral research. Direct PDF fetch unavailable; full indexed printed p. 138 checked, including political subordination, agricultural resurgence after 1910, colonial taxation/forced labor, later settlement and ecological pressure. Statements stay within that checked passage.

sources.title: Maria da Conceição Neto, Kuíto/Cuíto: historical background and urbanism, HPIP
sources.note: Scholarly built-heritage atlas, historical background directly indexed and read. Used for nineteenth-century Bié as a separate kingdom and caravan hub, named commodities and family settlements of outsiders.

sources.title: Museu Nacional, Getting to Know the Kumbukumbu Exhibition
sources.note: Original museum exhibition catalogue; indexed pp. 156 to 157 object list checked, identifying early twentieth-century wooden spoons, flour sieve, baskets and comb from the Celenia Pires donation. Dates describe objects and donation separately.

sources.title: British Museum, gourd rattle from a Dondi divination basket, Af1932,0514.53
sources.note: Full indexed original collection entry checked; direct fetch unavailable. Description: perforated gourd rattle, seed/gourd, 4.4 cm; Tucker notes dated 30 May 1932 call it Ochaka and connect it with keeping time to a diviner’s song. Museum ethnic field uses Mbundu, but acquisition text explicitly says Ovimbundu, Dondi.

sources.title: Royal Museum for Central Africa, Ovimbundu female figure EO.1967.63.208
sources.note: Original collection record, English and Dutch entries directly indexed and checked. Collected at Benguela by Robert Verly; acquisition 29 December 1967 does not establish manufacture date. Possible diviner use is explicitly tentative.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Keep separate broad Imbangala narrative. The sole world1815 feature has bounds [18.902,-10.9,20.137,-9.602], east of Cassange at approximately 17.8 E, 9.6 S in Livingstone. Kasanje is explicitly related context, not a verified polygon identity. Imported 1815 to 1878 interval is not a historical lifetime. No alias or successor added.

Distinct Bailundo kingdom; not an alias for the broad Ovimbundu record. Imported 1878 to 1914 polygon [14.089,-9.938,17.617,-7.706] is substantially north of documented Bailundo at about 12.195 S. Public overview warns of displacement. Period bounds use import window, not founding and fall. No shared narrative or successor link.

Treat as a broad community/political-region record, not a sovereign kingdom or alias of Mbailundu. Bounds [14.37,-13.11,16.263,-9.586], imported 1878 to 1914. Later fieldwork, objects and school publications are clearly dated beyond interval. No single fall date or successor link manufactured.
